findings.evidence: The proof identifies Imm(X×I,N) with paths in Imm(X,N). A smooth family is only slice-wise immersive; its derivative in the I direction need not be independent of the X derivatives. Take X=[0,1], N=R: Imm(X,R) is nonempty, but Imm(X×I,R) is empty by dimensions, so restriction cannot be a weak equivalence. Even for X a point and N=R, the fibre of Imm(I,R)→R has increasing and decreasing components. The opened def-compact-parameter-pair and smoothing lemma supply families, not immersions of the full product. Replace this with a collar extension of unchanged source dimension and prove the actual restriction homotopy equivalence; adding a target-dimension bound alone does not make the fibres contractible.

findings.location: Statement, analogous restriction on genuine immersions; Proof 4.1
findings.evidence: The unrestricted genuine-immersion Serre-fibration assertion is false. Let X=[-1,1], A=[-1,-1/2]⊔[1/2,1], N=R, with initial immersion the identity. On the left component set g_t(x)=x+2t and on the right set g_t(x)=x−2t. Every g_t is an immersion of A, but the endpoint reverses the order of the two images and cannot extend to a monotone immersion of X continuing the identity. Formal bundle monomorphisms can be perturbed linearly; genuine derivatives cannot be treated as arbitrary such sections. Francis, Lectures 5–6, p.1, Lemma 1.3 and Note 1.4 impose n>k and give the endpoint-swap obstruction. Remove or correctly restrict the genuine clause and prove its lifting statement with the required dimension hypotheses.

findings.location: Statement (ii), definition of Imm_ν and FImm_ν as subspaces
findings.evidence: Normal-bundle identification is additional data, not a property defining a subspace of the unframed immersion space. Francis, Lectures 5–6, p.3, Definition 1.8 uses pairs consisting of an immersion and a specified normal-bundle isomorphism; p.4 then uses the forgetful fibre bundles. As unframed subspaces, (ii) is false for M a point and N=R: Imm(D^1,R) has two orientation components whereas Imm(point,R)=R is contractible. Define the spaces of pairs and their topologies, retain the identification in restriction, and prove the corresponding forgetful-fibration comparison.

F1 supplies the disk-bundle manifold and the zero-section tangent-normal splitting, not a global horizontal splitting TD(ν)≅π*TM⊕π*ν; a connection or a proved splitting of the vertical tangent exact sequence is missing. Step 2.1 gives no explicit fibre contraction or fibration/homotopy-inverse argument; contractible fibres alone do not imply weak equivalence for an arbitrary map. Its cited Euclidean tubular results do not establish the extension into arbitrary N without the metric/exponential construction. Step 3.1 also relies on the false product-collar lemma. State AC_ω for the metric and open-source suppliers, prove the horizontal splitting and parametric exponential/shrinking construction, and replace the collar transfer. Francis Lemma 1.9, p.3, and the framed forgetful-fibration argument on p.4 identify the intended route but do not license the current shortcuts.
